questions.q: (a) Describe how a chain reaction occurs in a nuclear reactor [3]. (b) Explain the roles of the moderator, control rods and shielding [3]. (c) State one difference between fission and fusion [1].
questions.a: (a) U-235 absorbs a neutron and splits (1); releasing 2 or 3 neutrons (1); which go on to split other U-235 nuclei (1); (b) moderator slows neutrons (1); control rods absorb neutrons (1); shielding absorbs radiation to protect workers (1); (c) fission splits heavy nuclei, fusion joins light nuclei (1)

questions.q: Evaluate nuclear fission power for a country's electricity.
questions.a: No CO₂ during generation, reliable (1); radioactive waste lasts thousands of years, risk of accidents (1); judgement (1)

questions.q: Explain why the daughter nuclei of fission are radioactive.
questions.a: They have too many neutrons for stability, so they decay (usually by beta emission).

questions.q: Explain how control rods prevent the reaction running out of control.
questions.a: They absorb neutrons (1), so fewer neutrons cause further fissions (1)
questions.model: Chain reactions need neutrons. Rods soak up neutrons. Fewer neutrons, fewer fissions, slower rate.

questions.q: Why does fusion need a high temperature?
questions.a: Nuclei are positive and repel; they must move fast enough to get close and fuse
